problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=-\frac{5}{x}+2?$
worked_solution:
To plot $y=-\frac{5}{x}+1,$ we apply the following steps:

- Take the curve $y=-\frac{1}{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13934099/assets/9da0db2e6c97e507e82b7ca801e46802fabf91ad31ff53ad3cc9ae580151370a.png)

- Then, stretch the result by a scale factor of $5$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=-\frac{5}{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13934099/assets/4612933db2d25ce80b7e7258d3e381fd03f951246b515c3c34c69b71c537c7fc.png)

- Translate it by $2$ unit up to get the graph of $y=-\frac{5}{x}+2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13934099/assets/edb61b0239e926ae983d0cb67ffb05c7ff0b452564e6972dfa15cf0f2472a727.png)
